name: PSYC100 - Introduction to Psychology
description: Social influence, motivation, cognitive biases, and the psychology of decision-making

lessons.title: Week 7: The Invisible Forces
lessons.description: Social psychology, conformity, obedience, and influence

lessons.title: Week 8: Professional Success Psychology
lessons.description: Motivation theories, goal-setting, stress, and psychological safety

questions.question: What did Stanley Milgram's obedience experiments demonstrate?
questions.answer: People will obey authority figures even when asked to harm others, showing the power of situational pressure over individual morality
questions.explanation: 65% of participants gave lethal shocks when instructed by an authority figure

questions.question: What is the fundamental attribution error?
choices: Overestimating personality and underestimating situation when judging others
questions.answer: Overestimating personality and underestimating situation when judging others
questions.explanation: We attribute others' behavior to their character while ignoring situational factors

questions.question: What did Solomon Asch's line experiments show?
questions.answer: People conform to group opinions even when the group is obviously wrong; about 75% conformed at least once
questions.explanation: The conformity effect shows how social pressure influences our judgments

questions.question: What is the bystander effect?
choices: Less likely to help when others are present
questions.answer: Less likely to help when others are present
questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility makes individuals less likely to act when in groups

questions.question: What is cognitive dissonance?
questions.answer: Mental discomfort from holding contradictory beliefs/attitudes, leading us to change beliefs to reduce discomfort
questions.explanation: We lie to ourselves to maintain consistency between beliefs and actions

questions.question: How does social influence work in the digital age?
choices: Amplified through echo chambers, viral content, and algorithmic filtering
questions.answer: Amplified through echo chambers, viral content, and algorithmic filtering
questions.explanation: Digital platforms intensify conformity and influence through likes, shares, and recommendations

questions.question: What are the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
questions.answer: Bottom to top: Physiological, Safety, Love/Belonging, Esteem, Self-actualization
questions.explanation: Lower needs must be met before higher needs motivate behavior

questions.question: What are the three components of self-determination theory?
questions.answer: Autonomy, competence, relatedness
questions.explanation: These three psychological needs drive intrinsic motivation

questions.question: What makes goals effective according to goal-setting theory?
questions.answer: Specific, measurable, challenging but achievable, with commitment and feedback
questions.explanation: SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) improve performance

questions.question: What is self-efficacy?
choices: Belief in your ability to succeed at specific tasks
questions.answer: Belief in your ability to succeed at specific tasks
questions.explanation: Self-efficacy affects which tasks we attempt and how much effort we invest

questions.question: What is the difference between growth and fixed mindset?
questions.answer: Growth mindset: abilities can be developed through effort. Fixed mindset: abilities are innate and unchangeable
questions.explanation: Growth mindset leads to embracing challenges; fixed mindset leads to avoiding failure

questions.question: What is locus of control?
choices: Belief about whether you control outcomes (internal) or external forces do (external)
questions.answer: Belief about whether you control outcomes (internal) or external forces do (external)
questions.explanation: Internal locus: 'I control my destiny'. External locus: 'Life happens to me'

questions.question: What is flow theory?
questions.answer: Optimal experience when challenge matches skill level; characterized by deep focus, time distortion, and intrinsic enjoyment
questions.explanation: Flow occurs in the 'zone' between boredom (too easy) and anxiety (too hard)

questions.question: What does the ABCDE model help with?
choices: Managing stress by examining beliefs about events
questions.answer: Managing stress by examining beliefs about events
questions.explanation: Adversity → Beliefs → Consequences → Dispute → Energize; challenges irrational beliefs

questions.question: What is the Job Demands-Resources model?
questions.answer: Balance between job demands (stressors) and resources (support, autonomy). Imbalance leads to burnout or disengagement.
questions.explanation: Adequate resources buffer against demands; insufficient resources lead to stress

questions.question: What is psychological safety?
questions.answer: Team climate where people feel safe to take risks, speak up, and make mistakes without fear of punishment
questions.explanation: Psychological safety enables learning, innovation, and honest communication

questions.question: What is grit according to Angela Duckworth?
choices: Perseverance and passion for long-term goals
questions.answer: Perseverance and passion for long-term goals
questions.explanation: Grit predicts success beyond talent; it's about sustained effort over time

questions.question: What is imposter syndrome?
questions.answer: Persistent belief that your success is due to luck rather than ability, accompanied by fear of being exposed as a fraud
questions.explanation: Common among high achievers who discount their accomplishments

questions.question: What are heuristics?
choices: Mental shortcuts that simplify decisions but can lead to biases
questions.answer: Mental shortcuts that simplify decisions but can lead to biases
questions.explanation: Heuristics are fast and efficient but sometimes lead to systematic errors

questions.question: What is anchoring bias?
questions.answer: Over-relying on the first piece of information (the anchor) when making decisions
questions.explanation: Initial numbers influence estimates even when they're irrelevant

questions.question: What does framing effect demonstrate?
choices: How information is presented affects decisions, even when content is identical
questions.answer: How information is presented affects decisions, even when content is identical
questions.explanation: '90% survival rate' sounds better than '10% mortality rate' despite being the same

questions.question: What is prospect theory about?
questions.answer: People are risk-averse for gains but risk-seeking for losses; losses hurt more than equivalent gains feel good
questions.explanation: Losing $100 feels worse than gaining $100 feels good (loss aversion)

questions.question: What did Elizabeth Loftus discover about memory?
choices: Memories are easily distorted by suggestion and can be false
questions.answer: Memories are easily distorted by suggestion and can be false
questions.explanation: Leading questions and misinformation can create false memories that feel real

questions.question: What is inattentional blindness?
questions.answer: Failing to notice obvious stimuli when attention is focused elsewhere (e.g., gorilla in basketball game)
questions.explanation: We can miss dramatic events when our attention is engaged on something else

questions.question: What did the marshmallow test measure?
questions.answer: Delayed gratification and self-control
questions.explanation: Children who waited for two marshmallows showed better life outcomes, though results are debated

questions.question: What is the Dunning-Kruger effect?
questions.answer: Incompetent people overestimate their ability while experts underestimate theirs; lack of skill prevents recognizing lack of skill
questions.explanation: 'The more you know, the more you realize you don't know'

questions.question: How do emotions affect decision-making?
choices: Emotions guide decisions, can override logic, and affect risk perception
Emotions always lead to bad decisions
questions.answer: Emotions guide decisions, can override logic, and affect risk perception
questions.explanation: Emotions are integral to decision-making, not just noise to be eliminated

questions.question: What are the halo and horn effects?
questions.answer: Halo: one positive trait makes us view everything positively. Horn: one negative trait makes us view everything negatively
questions.explanation: First impressions or single traits color our overall judgment of people
